name: Magnus Moto
address: Na bulevaru od centra ka, Pete Proleterske Brigade,81000
description: We are exclusive importer/distributor for motorcycle brands: DUCATI, KAWASAKI, PIAGGIO, VESPA, APRILIA, MOTOGUZZI, KYMCO AND TRIUMPH. Helmets: AGV, SHOEI, KAPPAMOTO, GIVI and IXS. Motorcycle clothing/textile: DAINESE, IXS, GMS, HEVIK and GIVI. We also sell tire brand PIRELLI and METZELER. We also provide service and maintenance for our clients and walk-ins (if schedule permits).

name: Two Captains
description:
"Two Captains" – A cozy restaurant where sea and city meet. Enjoy fresh seafood and hearty dishes in a welcoming atmosphere, perfect for any occasion.
Restaurant. Bar. Author's cocktails.

name: Savina Forest
description: Savina Forest is a mesmerizing national forest located near Herceg Novi, Montenegro, renowned for its lush landscapes and natural beauty. This enchanting destination is a haven for nature lovers and adventure enthusiasts alike, offering a plethora of activities amidst its serene environment. As you wander through the forest, you’ll be captivated by the diverse array of flora and fauna that flourishes under the forest canopy. The vibrant colors and rich scents create an immersive experience that rejuvenates the spirit. For those who enjoy hiking, Savina Forest boasts numerous trails that cater to various skill levels, allowing visitors to explore the stunning scenery at their own pace. Along the paths, you might come across hidden gems such as tranquil streams, rocky outcrops, and panoramic viewpoints that offer breathtaking vistas of the surrounding landscape. Birdwatchers will delight in the chance to spot various species that inhabit the area, making it a perfect spot for photography and nature observation. In addition to hiking, the forest's peaceful ambiance provides an ideal setting for picnics, meditation, or simply unwinding in the embrace of nature. The fresh mountain air and the gentle rustle of leaves create a backdrop for relaxation and rejuvenation. Whether you’re seeking adventure or tranquility, Savina Forest is a must-visit destination that showcases the natural beauty of Montenegro, making it an unforgettable stop on your travel itinerary.

name: ADV Summit Montenegro 2025
description: International motorcycle festival with offroad routes, navigation courses and presentations. The event includes various activities such as rafting and test drives.

name: Aćimić Moto
description: Aćimić Moto is located in Podgorica and specializes in the sale of motorcycle gear, accessories and spare parts. The company works with global brands and offers a wide range - from helmets and apparel to motorcycle components. In-store you can receive professional advice on selecting equipment tailored to your riding style and skill level. They also offer servicing and support for your bike, making it a comprehensive solution for motorcycle enthusiasts. Its convenient location and well-known brand name convey a sense of reliability and professionalism.

name: PUB ROUTE 66
description: This bar is located not far from King Nikola's Palace. Here you can enjoy delicious pizza, club sandwiches, and cheeseburgers. Many customers say that PUB ROUTE 66 serves pretty good coffee. Visitors, however, don’t like the draft beer.

name: Blues bar
description: This bar is located not far from King Nikola's Palace. Here you can enjoy delicious pizza, club sandwiches, and cheeseburgers. Many customers say that PUB ROUTE 66 serves pretty good coffee. Visitors, however, don’t like the draft beer.

name: Marea Porto Montenegro
description: Marea offers a refined dining experience with stunning views of the superyacht marina. Whether for a sunset cocktail, a business lunch, or a gourmet dinner, the restaurant combines impeccable service with a sophisticated yet relaxed atmosphere.

name: Porto
description: Restaurant Porto is located in the heart of the city Podgorica, in the city center. The restaurant in Podgorica completely brought the spirit of the Mediterranean. Enjoy the beautiful ambience of the restaurant where olive trees, palm trees surround you.. Where you can try the most delicious seafood and taste premium wines.

name: Grill House Roštiljijada
description: Grill House Roštiljijada is located in Podgorica, at Goričani bb, and offers a cozy interior and welcoming atmosphere. The focus is on fresh, high-quality grilled dishes - large portions have become the restaurant’s trademark. The menu also includes traditional Montenegrin dishes, making it a great place to experience local cuisine. The restaurant has convenient parking and is located along the main road, perfect for travelers. It’s an ideal spot for a hearty lunch or dinner - delicious food at a fair price.

name: Moto Service BAGGI
description: Moto Service BAGGI is a professional motorcycle service center located on Nënë Tereza Street in Ulcinj, Montenegro. It specializes in repair and maintenance of all motorcycle brands and models, offering fast and reliable diagnostics. The shop is open until 6 PM and serves riders across southern Montenegro. For inquiries and appointments, you can contact them at +382 69 430 360.

name: Jasmin Bike
description: Explore Montenegro on two wheels with Jasmin Bike – rentals, tours, and total riding freedom. We offer reliable motorbikes, high-quality gear, and curated routes. No matter your experience level, there’s a perfect road waiting for you. Feel the wind, the thrill, and the open road!

name: RightRoute.me | Motorbike Rent & Tours
description: Discover Montenegro’s most scenic routes with RightRoute.me – Motorbike Rent & Tours. We offer top-quality bikes, full gear, and full support throughout your journey. Perfect for travelers seeking freedom and adventure. Book your ride today and feel the spirit of the road!

name: Herceg-Novi  Old Town
description: The Old Town of Herceg-Novi is a picturesque fortress on the Adriatic coast, founded in 1382 by Bosnian King Tvrtko I. It combines architectural elements from the Ottoman, Venetian, and Austro-Hungarian periods. Narrow streets, ancient churches, and fortress walls create a unique Mediterranean atmosphere. Today, Herceg-Novi Old Town is a popular tourist attraction and a cultural hub of Montenegro’s coast.

name: First view to Skadar Lake
description: A peaceful viewpoint offering a stunning first glimpse of the majestic Skadar Lake. From here, you can see the lake stretching far into the horizon, framed by gentle hills and lush greenery. Ideal for a quiet break during a trip — especially at sunrise or sunset when the landscape glows with soft golden light.

name: Perast Beach
description: A small and peaceful beach in the heart of Perast, right next to historical baroque buildings and a view of the famous islets — Our Lady of the Rocks and St. George. Great spot to relax after exploring the town. Crystal-clear water, cozy stone platforms, and a magical sunset over the Bay of Kotor.

name: Kotor Natural Beach
description: A small, quiet beach located near the Old Town of Kotor. Surrounded by natural greenery and calm waters of the Bay. Unlike popular tourist beaches, this one feels local and authentic. No loud music, no crowds — just nature and the sea.

name: Grga Moto d.o.o.
description: Grga Moto d.o.o. is a motorcycle gear and parts shop and service centre located in Podgorica. It offers a wide range of accessories, spare parts and equipment for motorcycles and ATVs. The company carries gear from many leading brands and provides expert advice on selection. The store also supports servicing and supplying replacement parts for motorbikes. Its convenient location and established name give clients a sense of reliability and professionalism.

name: Moto Soko
description:
Moto Soko is a well-known motorcycle service center in Montenegro offering a full range of repair and maintenance services. Riders can get professional help, as well as purchase parts and accessories for various models. Its convenient location and friendly staff make Moto Soko a great choice for bikers on the road.

ps:
Appointments recommended

name: Tuttomoto doo - SYM, ZONTES, MOTO MORINI
description: Tuttomoto doo is a dealership in Podgorica specialising in the brands SYM, ZONTES and Moto Morini, making it appealing for motorcycle enthusiasts. The showroom offers a wide range of new motorcycles and scooters, as well as accessories and components for enhanced ownership experience. Customers receive advice on selecting models, assistance with test rides and ongoing support after purchase.

name: Motorcycle repair shop "MotoMoosa"
description: Welcome to MotoMoosa, a trusted motorcycle repair shop in the heart of Montenegro! We offer professional service, diagnostics, and repairs for all types of motorcycles. Our skilled mechanics and high-quality spare parts ensure top performance. Ride Montenegro’s roads worry-free - we’ve got your bike covered!

name: Moto servis Batko
description: Moto Servis Batko is a fast and reliable motorcycle service center in Montenegro. We offer repairs, maintenance, and long-ride preparation for all types of bikes. Friendly staff, quality parts, and convenient payment options ensure your comfort. Stop by — your motorcycle will be in good hands!

name: Yamaha Motor - Montenegro
description: Yamaha Motor – Montenegro is located in Podgorica and serves as the official dealer of the Yamaha brand in Montenegro. A wide range of Yamaha motorcycles and scooters are available here, along with accessories and spare parts. The company offers both sales of new models and professional service in modern workshop facilities. The staff is focused on providing assistance and consultation, including model selection and ongoing support. A great option for anyone interested in top-quality motorbikes and looking for official-level service.

name: m17moto
description:
The company M17-Moto d.o.o. was founded in 2006 in Mostar.

We operate at Šehovina 26A on the M17 highway (Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina).

In addition to a wide range of motorcycle parts and equipment, we also offer our clients service for all types of motorcycles, quads, and jet skis. M17-Moto is a representative of renowned companies, and we provide our clients with only the highest quality. We are authorized representatives and distributors of Benelli motorcycles for Bosnia and Herzegovina as well as LS2 motorcycle equipment.

In addition to authorized dealerships, we represent brands such as MOTUL and ENEOS oils and lubricants, Regina chains, D.I.D., JT, FERODO discs, DYNAVOLT and LP batteries, DAYCO belts, MITAS tires, Shark and iSpido helmets, and many others.

In addition to the sale and distribution of motorcycles and motorcycle equipment, we are authorized service providers for most renowned motorcycle brands such as Honda, Yamaha, Kawasaki, etc.

name: ODISEJ Moto Shop
description: Odisej Moto-Shop is the official Honda motorcycle and scooter distributor in Bosnia and Herzegovina. You can find original Honda models, spare parts, and accessories, and benefit from expert advice and support. Riders value its service reliability and brand quality. A must-visit if you're a Honda enthusiast or need the assurance of OEM service.

name: Moto AB d.o.o. -Moto Kacige i Oprema za Motore Sarajevo. Rezevni dijelovi za motore i skutere
description: Welcome to Moto AB Sarajevo — a reliable biker’s shop in the city centre offering helmets, riding gear, spare parts, and quick service to get your bike ready for the next leg of your journey. Its convenient downtown location makes it a must-stop if you need consumables or protective gear on the road. Knowledgeable staff are on hand to help you select equipment or make modifications fast. A top choice to continue your adventure without unnecessary delays.

name: Mausoleum of Vladike Danilo
description:
The Mausoleum of Danila Petrovic-Njegos the founder of the ruling dynasty of Petrovic-Njegos - is located at the top of the Orlov krs (Orlov mountain), near the Cetinje Monastery.

The idea of constructing the mausoleum was first voiced by princess Elena, daughter of the king Nikola i Petrovic. She also came up with the blueprint for the monument. Construction work was complete in 1896, to the 200-year anniversary of the ruling dynasty of Petrovic-Njegos.

The monument has a dome-like roof supported by four columns. Under the dome is a stone sarcophagus with the remains of Danila Njegos. The sarcophagus is decorated with a relief image of the ruler, as well as symbols of cultural and political power — a cross, a circle and a flower. A memorial plate is also installed.

You can enjoy a spectacular view of Cjetine and the surrounding hills from the mausoleum site.

name: Fort Kosmacz
description: Fort Kosmač was the southernmost fortress in the Austro-Hungarian Empire, guarding the southern extremity of the border between the empire and Montenegro. It is situated near the village of Brajići, on a hilltop overlooking the road between Budva on the coast and Cetinje, the Montenegrin capital at the time. Constructed in the 1840s, it was attacked during an 1869 rebellion and was garrisoned by Austrian troops until the fall of the empire in 1918. After passing to the newly established Yugoslavia, it was garrisoned again by Italian troops for a period in the Second World War. The building is now abandoned and in a ruinous condition.

name: Ruins of Roman-era Necropolis
description:
The Ruins of the Roman-era Necropolis in Budva, Montenegro, offer a fascinating journey back in time to the Hellenic and Roman periods. The origins of this remarkable necropolis are intertwined with the construction of the "Avala" hotel, which took place between 1936 and 1938. During this process, archaeologists uncovered a treasure trove of historical artifacts and graves.

The necropolis is divided into two distinct periods. The older section dates back to the Hellenic period, spanning from the 4th to the 1st centuries BC, while the newer portion belongs to the Roman era, ranging from the 1st to the 2nd centuries AD. These two periods provide a glimpse into the changing civilizations that once thrived in this region.

It is estimated that the necropolis served its purpose for over a millennium, bearing witness to the passing of countless generations. Its longevity underscores its historical significance.

The excavation yielded a wealth of artifacts, including gold and silver jewelry, various types of dishe

name: Old Town of Bar
description:
The Old Town of Bar (Stari Grad Bar) is blessed with a privileged location: up on a hill, close to the Adriatic Sea, and guarded by the imposing Mount Rumija. It’s easy to figure out why so many rulers battled over its control.

From this cliff, located only four kilometres (2.5 miles) away from the shore, whoever was the boss of this powerful city would govern the affairs of whoever was in the vicinity.

name: Mausoleum Petar II
description:
The Mausoleum of Njegoš[a] is a mausoleum interring Petar II Petrović-Njegoš located on the top of Mount Lovćen.

The mausoleum is located twenty-one kilometres via asphalt road from near-by Cetinje and it was built on the idea of Croatian sculptor Ivan Meštrović. It was built on the same location of the Njegoš Testament Church which Njegoš had built in 1845 with the intention of being buried there and which he dedicated to his predecessor Petar I Petrović-Njegoš (who is canonized as Saint Peter of Cetinje in the Serbian Orthodox Church).

The church suffered damage from bombardment in both World Wars. In 1974, despite protest from the Metropolitanate of Montenegro and the Littoral and local Orthodox Christians, the old church was ordered demolished by a commission of the League of Communists of Montenegro led by Veljko Milatović and today's mausoleum was built

name: Gurdić Bastion
description: Is a circular defensive fortification that is part of the city walls of Kotor, Montenegro. It is located next to the Southern, or Gurdic, Gate and is named after the Gurdic River that flows nearby. The bastion was built to protect the entrance to the city and a strategically important passage.

name: Fortress of Herzog Stjepan Vukčić Kosača
description: Ljubuški Fortress, also known as Herceg Stjepan's Fortress (Croatian: Trvđava Herceg-Stjepana) or the Old town of Ljubuški (Croatian: Stari grad Ljubuški) is a medieval fortress in the municipality of Ljubuški, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

name: Stari Most Mostar
description: The Stari Most (Old Bridge) in the city of Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina, is a magnificent 16th-century stone arch bridge spanning the Neretva River. It became a symbol of the city and its name comes from the “mostari” (bridge keepers) who once guarded it. The bridge was destroyed during the war in 1993 and lovingly reconstructed in 2004, standing today as a symbol of peace and reconstruction. It is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a major tourist attraction.

name: Merdzan Glava Fortress (ruins)
description:
The Merdžan Glava Fortress was an Austro-Hungarian fortified military post east of Mostar.

It was built after the Austro-Hungarian occupation of Bosnia and Herzegovina . Mostar was a rear stronghold and had 19 fortified buildings, the most in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was a belt fortress , one of four built by Austria-Hungary in Bosnia and Herzegovina . The fortress on Merdžan glavi is 802 meters above sea level. At the foot of this fortress, a military camp was built in Opine (Lager Opine) as a logistical base for other fortresses on the hill.

Due to the need to access and visit this military station, as well as those on Svetigora (877 m) and Guberača (624 m), but also for the purpose of exploiting timber, Austria-Hungary with its existing expert staff made a way from Mostar along Fortica. They did not engage the local population. It led through Šipovac to Brasin. The branch led to Merdžan Head. It was also used for extracting forest materials from Velež. The road was asphalted after the Second World War, and it is said that it is the merit of Džemal Bijedić.

name: Stari Grad Blagaj, also known as Herceg Stjepan's Fortress
description: Blagaj Fortress or Old Town of Blagaj (Bosnian, Croatian and Serbian: Stari grad Blagaj, Serbian Cyrillic: Стари Град Благај; pronounced, locally known as Stjepan-grad, or Stipan-grad, in classical times Bona (Бона), is a town-fortress complex near the town of Blagaj, Bosnia and Herzegovina. The old Blagaj Fort was built on a high, inaccessible karst hill, at an elevation of 310 metres (1,020 ft) above sea level and 266 metres (873 ft) above the source of the river Buna. Blagaj Fort is 275 metres (902 ft) above sea level. Fortress is National monument of Bosnia and Herzegovina, declared by KONS on 6 December 2003.

name: Blagaj Tekke
description: Blagaj is a historic village and protected heritage site in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It is located in the south-eastern region of the Mostar basin, in the Herzegovina-Neretva Canton. It stands at the edge of Bišće plain and is one of the most valuable mixed urban and rural built environments in Bosnia and Herzegovina, distinguished from other similar built environments in its urban layout. Blagaj was most likely named for its mild weather patterns since blaga in Bosnian means "mild". Blagaj is situated at the spring of the Buna river and a historical tekija (Dervish monastery). The Blagaj Tekija was built around 1520, with elements of Ottoman architecture and Mediterranean style and is considered a national monument. Blagaj Tekke is a monastery built for the Dervish.

name: Old Town of Stolac
description: The Old Town of Stolac, also known as Vidoški, is located on a hill above the modern town and stands as one of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s most significant historical sites. Its architectural ensemble reflects nine distinct historical layers — from the prehistoric era and Illyrians to Romans, the medieval period, Ottomans, and Austro-Hungarians. The fortress walls, towers, and massive gate highlight its strategic importance: in the 17th century, it featured around 13 towers and was considered one of the largest fortifications in Herzegovina.

name: Belgrade Gate
description: The Belgrade Gate is located in the modern area of Belgrade and represents a historic entrance to the city’s fortified zone. It was built in the 18th century during the period of Austrian rule as part of the powerful defensive system surrounding the Petrovaradin Fortress. The gate’s architecture reflects the military and strategic needs of the time, with heavy stone masonry, a narrow passage, and fortified side towers. Today, the gate stands as both a historical monument and a symbol of continuity between Serbia’s defensive past and its vibrant cultural present.

name: Monument to Stefan Nemanja
description: The monument of Stefan Nemanja is located on Sava Square in Belgrade, in front of the former Main Railway Station. It is dedicated to the great prefect Stefan Nemanja, the ancestor of the Serbian medieval dynasty Nemanjići. It was erected on January 21, 2021.

name: Historical Museum of Serbia
description: The Historical Museum of Serbia is located at Trg Nikole Pašića 11 in the heart of Belgrade and is open to visitors from Tuesday to Sunday, from 12 pm to 8 pm. The museum was established on February 20, 1963, and houses more than 35,000 exhibits showcasing the history of the Serbian people from ancient times to the present day. Its collection includes archaeological discoveries, medieval artefacts, documents, and objects representing key periods of Serbia’s past. The museum frequently hosts temporary exhibitions on themes such as “Waiting for the Permanent Exhibition” and “Kings and Saints of Serbia.”

name: The Old Palace building in Belgrade
description: The Old Palace in Belgrade was the royal residence of the Obrenović and Karađorđević dynasties, located in the very center of the Serbian capital. It was constructed between 1882 and 1884, marking a period of modernization in Serbia’s history. The building is designed in the Neo-Classical style and is considered one of the most remarkable architectural works of 19th-century Serbia. Over time, the palace served not only as a royal residence but also as a parliamentary and administrative building until World War II. A visit here offers a glimpse into royal Serbia and shows how architecture once reflected the country’s spirit and aspirations.

name: Observation post of the Serbian Supreme Command on Kajmakčalan
description: In World War I, after crossing over Albania, where it was annihilated, the Serbian Army recovered after a while and occupied its position at the Macedonian front (Salonika front), which spread across the mountain Kajmakčalan in Маcedonia. On the top of this mountain there was the observation post of the Serbian Army High Command. It is located in the Pioneers Park.

name: Kalemegdan
description: Kalemegdan is a picturesque historic park and fortress in the heart of Belgrade, perched on a hill where the Sava and Danube rivers meet.The site has centuries-old history: once the Roman city of Singidunum, then successively fortified by Byzantines, Serbian despots, Ottomans and Austrians.The name “Kalemegdan” comes from Turkish: “kale” meaning “fortress” and “meçdan/megdan” meaning “field of battle.”Today the park includes tree-lined promenades, lookout points with sweeping vistas of the rivers and city, as well as museum spaces, ancient walls and gates from the fortress.It remains one of Belgrade’s favourite spots: locals and visitors alike come here in the evening to enjoy the sunset and the relaxed vibe.When you’re in Belgrade, a walk through Kalemegdan offers a perfect blend of nature, history and stunning urban views - an ideal place to unwind and get inspired.

name: Mechkin Kamen Monument
description: The Mechkin Kamen Monument perches on a cliff by Lake Ohrid, just 3 km from the city center, delivering bikers a thrilling ride along the winding lakeside road with panoramic sweeps over crystal-clear waters and Galichica Mountain peaks. This emblem of the 1903 Ilinden Uprising — a 12-meter statue of revolutionaries on Bear's Stone — lets motorcyclists park at the base and hike the path to the memorial overlooking Ohrid's 365 churches. It's a photo mecca — the dramatic crag with the monument crafts an epic shot of your bike against the sunset lake, with no barriers to edge closer. The vibe is heroic and serene: wave crashes mingle with mountain gusts, while locals share tips on Macedonian biker trails. Free entry, open 24/7, but aim for dawn or dusk — midday heat intensifies, and the path slicks after rain, so wear sturdy shoes.

name: Clock Tower
description: The Saat Kula Clock Tower rises in central Bitola on Magazia Square, offering bikers an easy ride through the bustling Vardar region streets with parking right at the base under shady plane trees. This 1830 Ottoman icon, a 30-meter tower with a clock, lets motorcyclists stash their bike and climb the steps for a panoramic city view from the top. It's a photo hotspot — the square-based arches with your motorcycle in the foreground against Balkan rooftops and Pelister Mountain peaks. The vibe is lively and nostalgic: the clock's chimes echo across the square, while nearby cafes beckon for coffee and tips on serpentine roads to Ohrid. Free entry, open 24/7, but hit it daytime — evening lights are magical, and summers sizzle, so grab water and soak in the 360-degree panorama.

name: Heraclea Lyncestis
description: The Heraclea Lyncestis Archaeological Site lies 9 km from Bitola at the foot of Pelister Mountain, delivering bikers a thrilling ascent via the serpentine Vardar highway with sweeping vistas over Lake Ohrid and mountain ridges. This ancient city founded by Philip II in the 4th century BC lets motorcyclists park right at the entrance and explore the 3,000-seat theater ruins, early Christian basilicas with mosaics, and city gates. It's a photogenic haven — the amphitheater steps and arcades craft a dramatic backdrop for your bike against Macedonian landscapes, with no crowds to disrupt meandering through the digs. The vibe is majestic and contemplative: olive winds whisper tales of Alexander the Great, while local guides share tips on Pelister biker trails.

name: Stobi Ancient Theater
description: The Stobi Ancient Theater sits along the Vardar River near Gradsko, 80 km from Skopje, giving bikers an easy off-ramp from E75 highway via twisty Vardar region roads with views over fertile valleys. This grand Roman structure from the 2nd century BC is part of North Macedonia's largest archaeological site, where riders can park right at the entrance and climb the amphitheater's tiers that once seated up to 800 spectators. It's a photogenic gem — the semicircular rows against the hills make an epic frame for your bike, with nearby basilica ruins and mosaics adding layers of ancient allure. The vibe is mystical and energizing: echoes of past applause blend with mountain winds, while local guides share tips on Balkan biker trails.

name: Bargala Archaeological Site
description: The Bargala Archaeological Site lies 12 km northeast of Shtip at the foot of Plachkovica Mountain, offering bikers a thrilling ride along winding roads in eastern Macedonia with panoramic views over the Bregalnica River. This fortified Roman-Byzantine city (4th–6th centuries AD) lets motorcyclists park right at the entrance and dive into history: explore the ruins of seven towers, two gates, and an early Christian basilica adorned with mosaics. It's a photogenic paradise — the trapezoidal fortress on the hill provides an epic backdrop for your bike against mountains and valleys, with no crowds to interrupt wandering the theater and residential quarters. The atmosphere is mysterious and invigorating: winds from Plachkovica carry echoes of ancient tales, while friendly local guides share tips on regional biker trails. Head there in spring or fall — summers are scorching, entry is free, but check hours (typically 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.) to catch the sunset over the ruins.

name: Archaeological Site Vardar Hill
description: Vardarski Rid is the central area of Gevgelija, which was continuously inhabited for more than 1000 years, from the end of the Bronze Age (13th century BC) to the arrival of the Romans (2nd-1st century BC). Through six successive settlements, starting from a small prehistoric settlement on Hill 1, during the 5th and 4th centuries BC the ancient Macedonian city grew - ancient Gortynia, a city attested in historical sources as one of the centers of Ancient Macedonia. After an interruption of the settlement for more than 1000 years, in the high Middle Ages (11th-13th centuries AD), the necropolis sector was again used for the burial of the population of Vardarski Rid. The findings discovered in the six of the researched sectors represent the remains of the ancient Macedonian city that existed (5th-1st century BC), and in the "Necropolis" sector there are burials from the oldest - initial settlement from the end of the Bronze Age (13th century BC) and from the youngest medieval horizon.

name: Povijesna jezgra Trogira
description: Trogir is a remarkable example of urban continuity. The orthogonal street plan of this island settlement dates back to the Hellenistic period and it was embellished by successive rulers with many fine public and domestic buildings and fortifications. Its beautiful Romanesque churches are complemented by the outstanding Renaissance and Baroque buildings from the Venetian period.

name: Venetian Tower
description: The Venetian Tower (Mletačka Kula) is the sole surviving remnant of a Venetian fortress constructed in 1441, located just south of Diocletian’s Palace. It stands on Braće Radić Square (Fruit Square), facing the waterfront promenade, making it a visible landmark in Split’s old town. The tower features an octagonal shape, robust stone construction, and traces of the original connecting castle walls. Although the interior is typically not open to the public, its exterior presence and historical significance make it a worthwhile “quick stop.” For motorbike travellers, it’s a convenient point — centrally located near Diocletian’s Palace and the waterfront, easily slotted into a coastal or historical route.

name: Diocletian's Palace
description: Diocletian’s Palace is an imposing Roman palace-fortress built by Emperor Diocletian at the turn of the 4th century. Listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site, it now forms roughly half of the Old Town of Split. Unlike many ruin sites, it’s a living part of the city: you’ll find cafés, shops and residences within its ancient walls. For motorbike travellers it makes a perfect stop: it’s centrally located, offers rich history and convenient access to further rides along the coast or inland. Allow about 30-45 minutes for the main sights inside.

name: Zlatna vrata (Porta Aurea)
description: The Golden Gate (Porta Aurea) was the main northern entrance to Emperor Diocletian’s Palace, built in the 4th century. Situated in the old town of Split, the gate impresses with its monumental façade, decorated arch and niches that once held statues of tetrarchs. For motorcycle travellers it’s a great stop: a historic landmark located centrally, with easy onward access to coastal routes and inland Dalmatia. The surrounding area is pedestrian-friendly, with cafés and shops, perfect for a brief rest and a look around after a ride. Allow around 15-30 minutes for photos and a quick stroll through the gate into the old town.

name: Roman City Ruins
description: The Salona Roman Ruins are the remains of a once-major Roman city, the capital of the province of Dalmatia, located just outside Split. Here you can explore parts of ancient walls, the forum, baths and other archaeological features — making it a compelling stop for travellers. The ride to the site follows scenic bends and coastal stretches — a great choice for bikers looking for a memorable waypoint. On-site you’ll find open-air ruins and walking areas where you can stretch your legs, take photos and soak up the atmosphere before heading back on the road. Note: this is not a high-lookout viewpoint, so allocate about 30-45 minutes to explore rather than linger for long.

name: Klis Fortress
description: Klis Fortress sits atop a rocky ridge near the village of Klis, just 12 km from Split. Built by Illyrians and reinforced by Romans and later Croatian nobles, it remained a strategic stronghold guarding the inland from the Adriatic coast for centuries. Today it offers breathtaking views of the sea, islands, and Split’s surroundings, making it a fantastic stop for riders and road-trip enthusiasts. It’s popular among motorcyclists thanks to the scenic climb to the fortress and its sweeping vistas. The site gained extra fame as a filming location for Game of Thrones.

name: Nutjak
description: Nutjak Fortress is perched on a steep cliff above the Cetina River, near Trilj, offering both a significant historical site and a spectacular viewpoint. Built in the late 15th century, the fort once defended against Ottoman raids, and today its ruins retain the atmosphere of ancient strongholds and raw nature. The ride to Nutjak winds through twisty mountain roads renowned among bikers for their scenic curves and river-canyon views. Upon arriving, there’s a short off-road/foot section from the car- or bike-friendly point to the ruins, but the vantage point at the top rewards the effort with wide vistas. A superb stop for a motorcycle route: combine the thrill of the road with the peace of a high-vista ruin.

name: Castle of Kruja
description: Kruja Castle is located in the town of Kruja on a scenic hilltop, commanding sweeping views of surrounding mountains and the Adriatic direction. Historically, it served as the stronghold of national hero Skanderbeg, who defended Albania against Ottoman incursions. Today the fortress houses museums, exhibits of historic arms, and ethnographic displays. It’s a well‑visited site, but the access road is often less busy, making it a pleasant stop for motorcyclists seeking historic sites. Strolling along the battlements, viewing platforms, and museums can take between 30 and 60 minutes, depending on how deeply you explore.

name: Preza Fortress
description: Preza Castle (Kalaja e Prezës) sits atop a hill overlooking the Tirana River, about 20 km northwest of the city. Built in the 15th century under Ottoman rule, the fortress has undergone several restorations and retains defensive towers and wall sections. The hilltop offers panoramic views of the Tirana valley and surrounding mountains. The access road features scenic curves, making it an appealing detour for motorcyclists — a mix of asphalt climb and descent with views along the way. Plan roughly 30 minutes for walking the fortress grounds and taking in photos.

name: The amphitheater in Durres
description: The Amphitheater of Durrës is one of the largest Roman amphitheaters in the Balkans, constructed in the 2nd century AD and designed to hold 15–20 thousand spectators. It sits centrally in Durrës, just a short walk from the coastline and port. On site visitors can explore remnants of the seating tiers, stage area, and underground passages beneath the arena. The location offers a striking historical contrast — ancient ruins amid sea, portfront, and modern urban life. For motorcyclists, it makes an ideal stop on a city route: wander through the amphitheater, grab a coffee, and then resume your journey out of Durrës.

name: Tomb of Kaplan Pasha
description: Kapllan Pasha’s Tomb is a small Muslim mausoleum located in the heart of Tirana, built in 1817. The structure is octagonal, standing on eight carved stone columns connected by arches. Originally, it was part of a larger cemetery complex associated with Tirana’s first mosque, which was destroyed during World War II; today this is the only tomb that remains. Kapllan Pasha himself was originally buried here, but his remains were later moved to Istanbul — so the tomb now functions more as a monument than a true resting place. For visitors it’s a small yet meaningful stop: its blend of Ottoman history set against Tiranë’s modern surroundings makes it a contemplative pause on a city route.

name: Piramide and Tiranës
description: The Pyramid of Tirana is a striking pyramid-shaped structure in Albania’s capital, originally opened in 1988 as a museum dedicated to the country’s communist leader. It has since been transformed into a cultural centre with cafés, exhibition spaces and an accessible roof platform offering broad views of the city. For motorbike travellers it works as a compelling stop: easy to access from central Tirana, a quick photo opportunity, a bit of city atmosphere before hitting the road. Parking may require navigating urban streets but it’s worth the short stop.

name: Rodoni Castle ruins
description: Rodon Castle (Kalaja e Rodonit) is a fortification constructed circa 1450-1452 on the Cape of Rodon, overlooking the Adriatic coast of Albania. Today, only fragments remain: outer walls, one tower and scattered ruins — part of the fortress has been swallowed by the sea due to coastal erosion. The setting is raw and atmospheric, ideal for a biker stop seeking nature, history and sweeping sea views. The access road features scenic curves and a quiet feel — perfect for a ride with a pause. Take about 20-30 minutes to walk the ruins, enjoy the vista and recharge before continuing your route.

name: Berat Castle
description: Berat Castle (Kalaja e Beratit) sits perched above the town of Berat in Albania, on a rocky hill overlooking the Osum River valley and surrounding hills. Its walls, largely built in the 13th century, rest atop fortifications that date back to the 4th century BC — testament to over two millennia of history. Inside the fortress you’ll find inhabited houses, Byzantine churches and the ruins of mosques, creating an atmosphere of living history. For motorbike travellers it’s a fantastic stop: the approach road offers scenic bends and a less-crowded route, and the short walk up rewards you with panoramic views and a blend of ride + culture.

name: The Sons Eatery
description: The Sons Eatery is located in StaroBarska Čarsija, Bar 85354, and is a convenient stop for bikers on the road. The restaurant offers fresh meals and drinks with fast service, so you can quickly continue your ride. Motorcycle parking is available nearby, and the location itself is a good spot for a short break while traveling through Montenegro.

name: Bokka Modern
address: Residence Teuta, Setaliste kroz Porto Montenegro.
description: Bokka Modern – A sleek and stylish dining destination where contemporary design meets innovative cuisine. The sophisticated ambiance, with its chic interiors and warm lighting, makes it perfect for date nights, special occasions, or indulging in Montenegro's vibrant culinary scene.

name: Verige 65
description: This elegantly designed restaurant represents simplicity of modern architecture with a deep respect for the nature around it. Made of glass, the interior creates a feeling of tranquility and profound connection with natural setting of the Boka Bay.

name: Pepe Nero
description: Indulge your senses by enjoying the specialties of the Mediterranean cuisine in a luxurious ambiance and environment. Our unique establishment is located in the heart of the Old Town of Kotor, at Milk Square, which adds a special touch to this wonderful story.

name: One
description: ONE Restaurant & Bar is located on the waterfront at the Porto Montenegro marina in Tivat and offers a luxurious seaside atmosphere. The menu combines modern Adriatic cuisine with international touches, prepared from fresh local ingredients. The interior is thoughtfully designed, featuring a spacious terrace by the dock, elegant décor, and a backdrop of yachts. The restaurant offers an excellent wine list, great attention to detail, and high-quality service, making it ideal for special occasions.

name: Il Pescatore, Porto Montenegro
description: Il Pescatore is located in the prestigious Porto Montenegro marina in Tivat, offering a modern seafood dining experience in a relaxed setting. The menu includes fresh fish, seafood, tuna and octopus burgers, as well as gluten-free options. The open and friendly interior features an open kitchen, warm design and a terrace overlooking the marina. Guests praise the freshness of the fish, creative signature dishes and attentive service. It’s a perfect spot for a light lunch or dinner with a view of the yachts - advance booking is recommended during the season.

name: INCONTRO BAR & FOOD
description: By day, it's the perfect spot for coffee and light bites; by night, the space transforms into a vibrant social hub with craft cocktails and shared plates that celebrate Montenegro's rich culinary heritage.

name: Restobar Taraca
description:
Suppose you’re looking for restaurants in Kotor with a view. In that case, our terrace offers a perfect spot to watch the moon rising over the San Giovanni Fortress while the river Škurda flows by, creating an ambiance of serenity and relaxation. We take pride in offering a diverse menu that caters to all tastes, including meat dishes, vegan and vegetarian options, pastas, pottages, and more!
Whether you’re a vegan or vegetarian, our restaurant’s got you covered with a large selection of plant-based dishes that are as delicious as they are healthy. We also offer an extensive selection of freshly squeezed juices and frappes to complement your meal.

name: Agape Porto Montenegro
address: Regent Pool Residences Baia, Porto Montenegro, 85320
description: Carefully designed interior, embellished with natural materials, will make you completely relax and indulge in enjoyment. A pleasant terrace by the sea, to fully enjoy the sunset.

name: Marenda Steak House
description: Marenda Steak House – Where fire meets flavor in the heart of Montenegro. This carnivore’s paradise specializes in premium grilled meats, from succulent ribeyes to traditional Balkan cevapi, all cooked over open flames for that perfect smoky char. The rustic-chic interior with its exposed brick and butcher-block accents sets the stage for a true meat lover’s experience.

name: Klopa
description: Klopa, located at Trg Fra Grge Martića 4 in Sarajevo, is a convenient stop for bikers looking for a quick bite. The restaurant serves a mix of local and European dishes, hearty snacks, and refreshing drinks. There’s a comfortable indoor area, and takeaway options make it easy for those on the road. Nearby parking allows for hassle-free motorcycle stops, and its central location is perfect for a short break before continuing your ride through the city.

name: Restoran Tavola
description: Restoran Tavola, located at Maršala Tita 50, Sarajevo 71000, is a good stop for bikers looking for a break, a meal, and a relaxed atmosphere. The restaurant serves Italian and Mediterranean cuisine: house-made pasta, meat and seafood dishes, risottos, and salads. The interior is pleasant, with a wine selection and attentive staff — great if you’re not in a hurry. It’s easy to reach from the city center, with public parking and nearby garages available. The restaurant is open roughly from midday until 11 PM, making it suitable for lunch or a late dinner.

name: Barba - Mediterranean Restaurant
description:
Restaurant Barba is a gathering place for all generations, and geographically speaking it is located in the very center of Sarajevo, halfway between Baščaršija and Ilidža. It is in a sufficiently accessible place, but at the same time away from the city crowds and everyday pace.
The diverse offer will satisfy everyone's taste, so you can try various Mediterranean specialties, from seafood to meat delicacies. With an excellent selection of wines and all other drinks, a quality time is guaranteed.

Whether you are looking for a light morning breakfast or a daily lunch, a relaxed or formal business dinner, or a dynamic fishing evening with live music, Mediterranean restaurant Barba is the place for you. Because as our guest says: Barba offers an escape from Sarajevo – in Sarajevo!

name: Restoran Zdrava voda
description:
Restaurant Zdrava voda is a private restaurant that has been operating since 1967. It is located on the M17 highway at the exit from Jablanica towards the Adriatic Sea. It is located in the Neretva canyon, in an oasis of silence and greenery.

On the menu you will find top-quality grilled specialties, a wide selection of dishes a la carte, fresh trout, and we especially highlight the famous Jablanica specialty, the famous lamb on the spit, which has become a kind of brand.

name: Restaurant Šadrvan
description: Located near the Old Bridge in Mostar, this traditional Bosnian restaurant is popular among tourists. It offers authentic local cuisine in a charming, historic setting — ideal for lunch or dinner after exploring the Old Town.

name: Restoran Kovačević
description: estoran Kovačević in Donja Jablanica (88420) is a great stop for bikers needing a solid meal and a break on the road. The menu features home-style and regional cuisine: grill items, young lamb roasted over spit, oven-baked dishes, cold starters, and drinks. The service is friendly, and the restaurant is open from early morning till late evening (roughly 7 AM to 11 PM). There’s spacious parking right next to the restaurant, clean toilets, and Wi-Fi available on-site. With a nice view over the river, it’s a relaxing place to rest before continuing your ride across Bosnia and Herzegovina.

name: Brunch Sa
description: Brunch Sa is a brunch cafe located in the historical centre of Sarajevo offering high-quality coffee and delicious brunch meals, pastries and cakes. We welcome you with a warm atmosphere.

name: Mezestoran Dvoriste
description: Hidden from the hustle and bustle of the city, exposed to fresh breezes from Crete, the Adriatic, Andalusia and the Middle East, "Mezestoran Dvorište" is a true gastronomic refreshment. It brings us simple, creative cuisine, which in its approach respects the rules of the Mediterranean diet, philosophy and way of life.

name: Casa Nova
description:
Casa Nova is not just a restaurant – it is a story told through a space that exudes warmth and an artistic touch. Every detail in the interior has been lovingly crafted, so that guests feel like they have stepped into a space that inspires them and takes them on a journey.

Inspired by Tuscany and the Mediterranean regions, our ambiance features Botticelli-style frescoes, walls that carry the spirit of the 14th and 15th centuries, and an atmosphere that invites enjoyment.

Here, past and present dance in perfect harmony.

name: Franš Restaurant Belgrade
description:
Where modern elegance meets timeless Serbian hospitality.
Sophisticated urban ambiance with warm, attentive service
Contemporary twists on Balkan classics using seasonal ingredients
Curated Serbian & international wine pairings

name: Bela Reka Restaurant
description:
Once upon a time, every dish was known for its good recipe,
fresh local ingredients, prepared with lots of love.
At the national restaurant "Bela Reka" it is still known today!
Inspired by the proven recipes of our grandmothers,
we open a treasure trove of unforgettable local flavors.
The restaurant "Bela Reka" is a place of exciting gastronomic
encounters of tradition and modernity, local and national,
homely and cosmopolitan.
A place where you can relax and enjoy, where you can eat well
and where the finest wines or brandies are poured.
It is a place that will awaken all your senses.
But "Bela Reka" is, above all, your second home.

Welcome!

name: Three sheshiras
description: "Tri šešira" is a real pearl among the restaurants of Skadarlija. It was built in the heart of Skadarska Street and has existed in a recognizable atmosphere for more than 150 years. It was opened in 1864 in a building that previously housed a craft workshop, which had three tin hats as its logo. That is how the restaurant got its name. The restaurant is known for its service and quality even beyond the borders of our country. It had the honor of hosting the most eminent domestic and international personalities: King Juan Carlos, George Bush, Pertini, Willy Brandt and others. Testimonies of a pleasant stay in the restaurant are kept in the guest book.

name: Buena Vida Beograd
description: Buena Vida is more than great Mexican food; it provides a space to make memories. We pride ourselves in guiding customers through a curated menu, going beyond the expectations of hospitality, and leaving them to enjoy the company they are with.

name: Bistro Grad Hometown Food
description:
Choose a place and treat your palate to a wide variety of Balkan and Mediterranean delights, vegan or meat specialties, soups, omelettes or grilled fish – strictly according to grandma's recipe!

For carefully selected homemade brandies or craft beers, choose the elegant bar on the ground floor. Or take your drink upstairs and relax in our lounge upstairs.

name: Durmitor
description:
The Durmitor national cuisine restaurant opened its doors in 1993 in the center of New Belgrade and in a short time stood out with its exceptional service, high-quality, fresh food and exceptional wine selection.
Here, homemade bread is baked every day, homemade cakes are prepared, and specialties that are talked about are enjoyed in the pleasant ambiance of the restaurant, which has long been recognized by business and family people.
In the Durmitor restaurant, which has a family tradition, veal, lamb and kid under the oven, cooked dishes, barbecue, fish specialties are prepared every day, and one of the dishes that is talked about is steak in olive oil. The restaurant's working hours are from Monday to Saturday from 8:00 to 23:00. (the restaurant is closed on Sundays).
Check out why more people are looking for a place here!

name: Comunale Caffe e Cucina
description:
Comunale Caffé e Cucina is one of the first restaurants responsible for transforming the previously abandoned and forgotten Beton Hala into what is now a cult venue on the Belgrade gastronomic scene and an unmissable tourist destination on the banks of the Sava River. We have been proudly serving our guests since 2010, with an offer that includes the best of Italian and Mediterranean cuisine combined with the finest from Josper Grill, along with a unique bar offering and our very carefully selected wine list. All this with a very discreet creative flair in a unique interior because we want only the best for you.

A place where you eat. Where you discover experiences. Where you enjoy.

name: Soul Kitchen - Macedonian Wine & Cuisine
description:
Nestled in Skopje’s Old Bazaar, Soul Kitchen is a celebration of Macedonian heritage through food and wine. The menu stars rustic dishes like tavče gravče (baked beans in clay pots), succulent kebabs, and flaky burek, paired with local wines like Smederevka and Temjanika.

The rustic-chic interior, adorned with walnut wood accents, sets the stage for a memorable dining experience. Guests rave about the warm service, homemade lepinja bread, and the restaurant’s commitment to authenticity – even supporting elderly flower sellers nearby. A must-visit for foodies exploring North Macedonia’s soulful cuisine

name: Restaurant Skopski Merak
description:
The restaurant Skopski Merak was launched on May 21st 1991 in an old house on the Andon Dukov street in the Debar Maalo region of Skopje. We started with 5 tables and 20 plastic chairs and from which in 2011 we proudly opened the new Skopski Merak on the popular street Debarca, also in Debar Maalo
Nestled in Skopje’s vibrant Debar Maalo district, Skopski Merak has been a cornerstone of Macedonian dining since 1991. This family-run gem blends rustic charm with culinary tradition, offering slow-cooked dishes like wood-fired pastrmajlija (Macedonian "pizza") and succulent 8-hour roasted ribs. Pair your meal with premium local wines, such as Kamnik Winery’s Reserva Merlot, while live folk music enhances the warm, convivial atmosphere.

Praised for its friendly service and affordable prices (a full meal with wine averages €25–€65), the restaurant caters to all diets with vegan, gluten-free, and hearty meat options. Don’t miss their clay-pot specialties or the legendary Grandmother’s Cake for dessert

name: Restaurant “Old House”
address: Boulevard Phillip the Second of Macedon 14, 1000
description: Nestled in the heart of Skopje, Restaurant „Old House“ (also known as Stara Kuka) is a culinary gem housed in a meticulously preserved 19th-century traditional building. Renowned for its warm ambiance and dedication to Macedonian heritage, this restaurant offers an immersive dining experience where folklore decor, live traditional music, and a courtyard fountain transport guests to another era

name: Kolektiv (Collective) Restaurant
description: Located on Macedonia Square in central Skopje, Kolektiv (Collective) Restaurant is a lively spot blending international cuisine with a craft beer focus. The industrial-chic space features exposed brick walls, communal tables, and outdoor seating overlooking the square’s iconic fountain

name: La Terrazza Restaurant
description: Located just steps from Macedonia Square in Skopje, La Terrazza Restaurant blends authentic Italian cuisine with a touch of Balkan flair. Known for its wood-fired pizzas and generous portions of shopska salad, this spot attracts both locals and visitors—including politicians from the nearby Parliament building

name: Restaurant “Kantina”
description: Located in the heart of Skopje, "Kantina" is a contemporary restaurant that reimagines traditional Balkan cuisine with a creative twist. Housed in a stylishly renovated space, it offers a refined dining experience where local ingredients meet innovative techniques.

name: Amigos Mexican Restaurant and Bar
description: Discover the world of flavors in the heart of Skopje. Whether on the terrace or inside, enjoy every bite of the specialties inspired by Mexican culture with a modern twist. And then, join us at the bar with unique signature cocktails and surrender to the moment!

name: National Restaurant Makedonska Kukja
address: Teodosie Gologanov no 63 nearby Alumina, Mitropolit Teodosij Gologanov, 1000
description: Located in the heart of Skopje, Makedonska Kukja is more than just a restaurant—it’s a living museum of Macedonian culture. Housed in a traditional-style building, the venue showcases centuries-old artifacts, creating an immersive atmosphere where diners can enjoy authentic Macedonian cuisine accompanied by live folk music and dance performances

name: Gino Italian Restaurant
description: Located in GTC Shopping Mall, Gino Italian Restaurant is Skopje’s first original Italian eatery, founded in 1997 by Tuscan chef Gino Guacini. Renowned for its handmade pasta, wood-fired pizzas, and homemade ice cream, this restaurant blends Italian authenticity with Macedonian hospitality. The menu features Tuscan specialties like fresh gnocchi, ravioli, and cannelloni, crafted daily with durum wheat flour and local ingredients

name: Bokeria Kitchen & Wine
description: Inspired by Barcelona’s famed La Boqueria market, Bokeria Kitchen & Wine is a culinary gem in Split’s old town, blending Mediterranean flavors with modern flair. The two-story space dazzles with a mosaic-tiled bar, shelves stacked with wine bottles, and a dramatic chandelier suspended from an 850-meter chain

name: Konoba Karoca
description: Tucked away in Crikvenica, Konoba Karoca is a hidden gem celebrated for its hearty Croatian dishes and warm, rustic ambiance. Despite its unassuming exterior, the restaurant delights guests with generous portions of fresh seafood, grilled meats, and homemade specialties.

name: Boban
description: A cornerstone of Zagreb’s fine dining scene since 1995, Restaurant Boban blends Italian culinary artistry with Croatian hospitality. Named after the legendary Croatian footballer Zvonimir Boban, this sophisticated venue is famed for its handmade pasta, truffle dishes, and an extensive wine cellar featuring 450+ labels.

name: Dalmatino Dubrovnik
description: At Dalmatino Dubrovnik, we are very passionate about our work. All our team members strive to make Dalmatino the best restaurant in Dubrovnik. For example, one of our dining halls is located at the place where the old Dubrovnik's bakery used to be. Dining in this room you can experience Dubrovnik's history. The room displays a large baking oven, made of clay bricks, giving that special something to the experience. Walls are decorated with large format paintings from local artists, introducing insight into Dubrovnik's artistic world. Street seating is very atmospheric and provides the summer hustle and bustle of Dubrovnik’s streets. Besides the ambience that the Dubrovnik old city provides, one of our most important traits are our employees, professional and friendly.

name: Nautika
description:
Nautika Restaurant lies on the very edge of the sea at Pile, alongside the western entrance to Dubrovnik's Old City.
From its unique terraces, diners can enjoy a truly one of a kind view of the Adriatic and the fortresses of Lovrijenac and Bokar. The restaurant's chef, Mario Bunda, leads a team whose varied offerings include lobster from the Dalmatian island of Vis and delicacies from the local waters of the Adriatic.
The restaurant is housed in the former Dubrovnik School of Maritime Studies, where it welcomed famous seafarers since as far back as 1881. Today the restaurant serves to preserve the location's rich history, while retaining the noble atmosphere of Dubrovnik's reign as a republic. In 2008. Nautika Restaurant was recognized as the sixth most romantic restaurant in the world by the much respected Condé Nast Traveller magazine. Nautika was honoured to host Saint John Paul II on June 6th of 2003.

name: HERITAGE - Croatian Street Food & Shop
description:
Visit Heritage Croatian street food where you can explore the origins of our fresh, local ingredients.
Join us on a journey through the heart of Croatia’s finest flavors.

name: Konoba Tarsa
description: Nestled in Rijeka’s charming Trsat district, Konoba Tarsa is a rustic tavern celebrated for its homemade Croatian dishes and warm, convivial atmosphere. Housed in a historic building with exposed brick walls and wooden beams, this family-run spot blends tradition with generous hospitality.

name: Bistro Riva
description: A quaint bistro along the Adriatic coast in Sveti Juraj, Bistro Riva offers simple yet satisfying meals with a focus on fresh, local ingredients. While the menu details are currently unavailable, it’s known for its relaxed seaside vibe and proximity to scenic spots like the Senj Hydroelectric Power Plant and the islet of Lisac

name: Restoran Ambar
description:
We believe that everyone should experience Croatia in all its essence and beauty, that is why we offer authentic local cuisine from fresh and organically sourced ingredients. You can choose homemade dishes from our menu, carefully designed by one of the best Croatian chefs Mate Janković.

Simple and modern, each meal shows the quality of our service and effort made into making your dining experience an unforgettable one.

name: Restorant Tymi
description:
Tymi (meaning "Smoke") is a no-frills, traditional Albanian grill house specializing in wood-fired meats and classic Balkan flavors. Known for its smoky aromas and generous portions, this casual spot is a favorite among locals for quick, delicious meals.
Why Visit?
🍖 Signature Dishes:
Qebapa (grilled minced meat skewers)
Mish në hell (slow-cooked lamb or beef)
Suxhuk (spicy homemade sausages)
🔥 Cooking Style: Charcoal-grilled meats with a smoky finish.

name: Gjelltore SaUku - Traditional Albanian Cuisine
description: A family-run gem in Tirana, Gjelltore SaUku is celebrated for its homemade Albanian cuisine and warm hospitality. The restaurant’s rustic charm and generous portions make it a favorite among locals and tourists alike.

name: Makamona Restaurant
description: Nestled away from tourist crowds, Makamona Restaurant offers an intimate dining experience with a focus on Albanian and Mediterranean cuisine. Praised for its fresh ingredients, attentive service, and cozy ambiance, it’s a favorite among locals and visitors alike.

name: Temi Albanian Food
description: Nestled within Berat Castle, a UNESCO World Heritage site, Temi Albanian Food is a family-run restaurant celebrated for its homemade Albanian cuisine and warm hospitality. The cozy, rustic ambiance—featuring wooden furnishings and traditional decor—creates an inviting atmosphere reminiscent of an Albanian home

name: Fresh Garden Restaurant
address: Rruga Brigada VIII Ndertesa 8, H16, Ap1, 1019
description: Ranked among Tirana’s Top 5 restaurants, Fresh Garden Restaurant blends Italian-Mediterranean flavors with Albanian hospitality. Known for its impeccable service, complimentary treats (like limoncello shots), and lush greenery-adorned ambiance, it’s a favorite for romantic dinners and family gatherings alike

name: Mrizi i Zanave Tirane
description:
Restaurant “Mrizi i Zanave”, operating since 2004, is located in the center of Tirana, next to the 18th century monument Ura e Tabakeve (Tanners’ Bridge). It was named “Mrizi i Zanave” in memory of the owner’s grandfather, Brahë Alia, who sang on the Albanian lute of fairies (Zana) resting near streams in the high oak forests (Mrizi) and the legendary brave warriors defending their highlands through the epic verses of the Songs of the Frontier Warriors.

The tranquil purity of the fairies and the relentless fighting spirit of the heroes we aim to bring to you through the interior built with wood and rock from Valbona, artisanal works from Zadrima, Kruja and Korça, and the combination of traditional highland dishes made of organic products from the Albanian Alps with modern Mediterranean cuisine.

name: EJA RESTAURANT
description: Nestled in the heart of Tirana, EJA RESTAURANT offers a contemporary take on traditional Albanian cuisine. The restaurant's sleek, minimalist design contrasts beautifully with its rustic flavors, creating a unique dining experience that bridges past and present.

name: Balcony Restaurant
description: Perched above Sarandë’s bustling waterfront, Balcony Restaurant lives up to its name with cliffside terraces offering uninterrupted sea views. This upscale seafood spot blends Albanian hospitality with Mediterranean flavors, perfect for sunset dining.

name: Restaurant Metropol traditional Albanian and Italian dishes
description:
Blending the heartiness of Albanian cuisine with Italian culinary finesse, Restaurant Metropol offers a unique gastronomic experience. The menu celebrates both cultures through:

Albanian Specialties:
Tavë Kosi (baked lamb with yogurt)

Fërgesë (pepper and cheese stew)

Italian Classics:
Handmade Pappardelle with wild boar ragù
Seafood Risotto al Nero

name: Panorama Lake Viewpoint with Cafe
description: The Panorama Lake Viewpoint with Café is a hidden gem located in the heart of Montenegro, offering visitors a spectacular vantage point to soak in the breathtaking beauty of the surrounding landscape. Perched high above the serene waters of the lake, this viewpoint is perfect for those looking to escape the hustle and bustle of everyday life. The stunning vistas stretch for miles, showcasing the lush greenery of the mountains and the tranquil blue of the lake below. It’s an ideal spot for photography enthusiasts eager to capture the incredible scenery.

name: Picturesque viewpoint
description: The Picturesque Viewpoint is a must-visit destination for anyone traveling to Montenegro, renowned for its breathtaking views that capture the essence of this beautiful country. Perched atop a scenic overlook, this tourist attraction offers a stunning panorama of the verdant valleys below, framed by majestic mountains that seem to stretch endlessly into the horizon.

name: Valovito Lake Point View
description: Surrounded by rocks and cliffs, the Valovito Lake is located near the Modro and Srablje Lakes at an altitude of 1.695m.

name: Piva lake viewpoint
description: Nestled in the heart of Montenegro, the Piva Lake Viewpoint is a captivating destination that enchants visitors with its stunning scenery and serene environment. This picturesque spot offers breathtaking panoramic views of the shimmering turquoise waters of Piva Lake, set against a backdrop of majestic mountains and lush greenery.

name: Balkan Moto Travel
description: We are a motorcycle rental agency and also provide tailor-made tours in Montenegro, Albania, Croatia and the Balkans. We pride ourselves on a high level of customer service and have a fleet of brand-new adventure bikes and roadsters with comprehensive insurance.

name: Biker Bar
description: Biker Bar is a popular local hangout known for its welcoming staff and lively atmosphere. Visitors frequently praise the café’s quick and attentive service, making it a favorite stop for both regulars and travelers.

name: Montenegro ride
description: Discover the Balkans with our boutique style motorcycle tours. Based in beautiful Montenegro, we offer guided tours, self-guided tours, and motorcycle rentals tailored to solo riders, couples, and groups. Whether you're exploring Montenegro’s scenic roads or venturing into Croatia, Bosnia, or Albania, we’re here to help you to create memorable motorcycle adventures. Join our guided tours to experience Montenegro through local insights or rent a motorcycle for a self-paced journey. We’ve mapped out the best routes, hotels, and must-see attractions to ensure a seamless and memorable ride.

name: The Nitrox Pub & Eatery
description:
"The Nitrox” is a special diving technique, where a combination of Nitrogen and Oxygen is used by professional divers to stay longer under the sea. Just like you would like to stay more at our pub!

Operating in a friendly attitude, relaxed and professional atmosphere we are eager to meet you and share our previous experiences making every journey inspiring for years to come.

name: Motorcycle Rental Pravo - Iznajmljivanje Motora Beograd
description:
Explore Belgrade and beyond with ease by renting a motorcycle from Pravo. Choose from a variety of well-maintained bikes, including scooters and touring models, perfect for both city rides and longer road trips through Serbia and the Balkans.

All rentals include helmets, insurance, and flexible rental periods. Whether you're a solo traveler or exploring with friends, Motorcycle Rental Pravo offers reliable service, competitive prices, and local tips to make your ride unforgettable.
